content.text:
I couldn't find anything in the site to fix, so I haven't changed any files. All 12 visual tests (6 pages × desktop and phone) still fail. As far as I can tell, the differences come from how the browser draws text on this machine, not from a change to the site.

**What the differences are:**
- On every page they're a thin scatter along the soft edges of letters. Letter shapes, positions, layout, spacing and colours all match the approved screenshots; solid text is still exactly `--color-ink` (#1f2328).
- Only 19–100 pixels per page cross the test's failure threshold. Zoomed in 10×, the approved and new home-page heading look the same.
- The renders are stable: two runs back to back differed by at most one colour level on a few pixels.

**Why I don't think the site's code caused it:**
- Nothing in the CSS, HTML, `app.js` or `server.js` changes how text is drawn: no opacity, filters, text-shadow or font-smoothing rules.
- I rendered the home page with several text-rendering CSS changes. Turning off kerning or switching to `geometricPrecision` produced much bigger differences (letters moved, up to 218/255 colour change). The rest had no effect. So a real CSS change would have looked very different from what the tests show.
- The repo has a single commit, so I can't see what the "last change" was or compare against it.

The most likely cause is that the approved screenshots were made with a different browser build or font renderer than this machine's (Playwright 1.63). I can't confirm that, because I don't have the setup that made them.

**Options:**
1. **Re-approve the screenshots** with `npx playwright test tests/visual.spec.ts --update-snapshots`. This overwrites the approved images, so it only makes sense if you agree nothing really changed. I didn't want to do that without asking.
2. **Allow a little tolerance** in `tests/visual.spec.ts` (e.g. `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.001`) so small text-edge differences don't fail the tests. Real layout or style changes would still be caught.
3. **Tell me what you noticed.** If you saw a specific change (a page, element or colour), I'll look there. It might be something these screenshots don't capture, such as hover states or the mobile menu when open.

STATUS: NOT DONE
